Subject: Recap + next steps — SLOs, streaming, and token bounds

Hey Jordan — thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned acceptance criteria for the perf qualification run. Attached: acme_slo_requirements.xlsx and sample_payloads_v2.json.

Key points we captured:
- Expected traffic pattern: baseline 15 rps sustained during peak, burst to 60 rps for short windows (~10–15 min).
- Typical input sizes: median ~400 tokens, 90th percentile ~2.1k tokens; occasional long-context inputs up to ~12k tokens (historical batch uploads).
- Expected output lengths: conversational replies median ~120 tokens, but some generation flows produce multi-turn summaries up to ~6–8k output tokens.
- Desired latency targets: p95 interactive responses under 400 ms for short prompts (<1k tokens). For long outputs we are OK with streaming, but first-byte latency needs to be < 250 ms and steady token-streaming throughput should keep tail completion reasonable.
- Concurrency requirement: 200 concurrent end-users, average session multiplexing ~3 live requests per user.

Open questions from our side to finalize the test plan:
1) Confirm the token distribution (if you can drop a sample histogram we can map to our batching logic).
2) For long-output flows, do you require full message atomicity (all-or-nothing) or is partial/streamed content acceptable?
3) Any specific privacy constraints for sending representative payloads to Redwood's dedicated perf cluster?

Proposed next steps:
- You: send a small sample (<= 5 MB) of anonymized requests with token counts/histogram.
- Us: run two qualification sweeps on Dedicated-equivalent bones: (A) short-path p95 latency profile (no streaming) and (B) streaming-enabled long-output throughput + first-byte latency.
- Joint call: 60-min perf session next week to review run, share traces, and finalize tuning (quantization, batch sizing, cache suggestions).

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- Short-path p95 <= 400 ms for inputs <= 1k tokens at baseline throughput.
- For outputs > 2k tokens, streaming first-byte < 250 ms and sustainable token emission >= 200 tokens/s on our suggested config.
- End-to-end error rate < 0.5% and no timeouts at sustained burst.

If that looks right, I’ll schedule the perf test and add Marissa (SE) and Rishi (SRE/lead) to the session.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Perf plan: measurable tests, configs, and scripts

Jordan / Priyom — quick technical plan from the SE side so you know exactly what we’ll execute during the qual run. I added some explicit knobs so procurement has concrete artifacts.

Planned qualification sweeps:
- Sweep A (short-path latency):
  * Payloads: 1k synthetic samples drawn from your histogram (median and 90th included).
  * Mode: non-streaming, batching tuned for p95 latency.
  * Goals: p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, per-request token cost.
- Sweep B (streaming long-output):
  * Payloads: 10 long-output traces (2k–8k expected output).
  * Mode: streaming enabled; we measure first-byte latency, steady-state token rate, and end-to-end completion time.
- Sweep C (batch/analyze worst-case):
  * Payloads: a handful of 10–20k token jobs to validate isolation from interactive traffic.

Configuration candidates we’ll test (examples):
- Model family: raven-13b-quant vs raven-70b-ptq.
- Quantization: int8 + KV-cache optimizations.
- Batching window: 4–30 ms (we’ll sweep to find the knee for p95).
- Stream chunk size: 64–256 tokens for balancing throughput vs latency.

Measurement artifacts we’ll produce:
- Per-request trace with timestamps for request received, kernel launch, first-byte, last-byte.
- Token emission rate trace for streaming.
- Load profile (RPS/concurrency) and resource utilization.
- Short report with recommended config and estimated per-token cost at observed throughput.

Acceptance criteria (concrete version we’ll report on):
- Short-path: p95 <= 400 ms at baseline load (15 rps) and p95 <= 650 ms at burst target (60 rps).
- Streaming: first-byte < 250 ms; steady-state >= 200 tokens/s on the chosen config for outputs > 2k tokens.
- Batch isolation: interactive tail latency not increased by > 15% when large batch jobs are running in parallel.

Logistics / next steps:
- Jordan: share the anonymized sample CSV and confirm redaction rules.
- Jordan: add procure@acme.ai if procurement needs to attend the review.
- Priyom: confirm a 60-min slot (I propose Tue 4/13 10:30 PT).

I’ll also prepare a short runbook and the perf scripts (we’ll share the repo link before the session).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
